metadata.case_name: WONG ELEVEN v. CHINA WAY TRANSPORTATION LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Driver for various charitable organizations; part-time camp instructor for The Hong Kong Federation of Youth Groups (teaching adventure courses); self-employed van driver cum delivery worker
plaintiff.occupation_after: Resumed first two part-time jobs with some modification of duties

injuries.description: soft tissue injury to the neck (sprain neck) with residual mild neck and left upper trapezius pain
source: The provisional diagnosis was sprain neck.
Dr. Lam’s diagnosis was soft tissue injury to the neck
injuries.icd_description: Other specified strain or sprain of cervical spine

manifestations.description: Tenderness at the left trapezius muscle at the neck.
Neck pain (residual mild neck and left upper trapezius pain).
Muscle guarding over the left cervical paraspinal muscle and left upper trapezius

treatments_received.treatment: A&E attendance and ambulance transfer to North District Hospital
source: After the accident, the plaintiff was sent to A&E Department (“A&E”) of the North District Hospital (“NDH”) by ambulance from the scene[16].
He was treated with analgesic, and a neck collar given[17].
He was treated with analgesic, and a neck collar given[17].

treatments_received.treatment: Three days' sick leave (granted on discharge)
source: He was discharged on the same day with three days of sick leave granted.[18]

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Residual neck and left upper trapezius pain may cause him minor discomfort and diminish his enjoyment of some of these sports or outdoor activities
